sampling_model.design: \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,Z_i,X_i)\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), with fixed \(K\) and a fixed number of cross-fitting folds.
sampling_model.units: Independent study participants with bounded continuous outcomes and pretreatment covariates.
sampling_model.treatment: \(J_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\) is latent and ordered; \(A_i\) and \(Z_i\) are paired categorical measurements.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Training-fold estimation uses one coherent label-aligned product factorization; all posterior, projector, and Gram quantities are plug-in implications of that fitted law.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: As the discretization becomes sufficiently fine, the approach recovers the efficiency bound asymptotically.
A valid influence function is obtained for categorical hidden actions using inverse-feature product bridges.
The parameters of the model are uniquely identifiable, up to label swapping.
The estimators are efficient if computed under the truth.
We present a constructive identification argument and use it to develop simple two-step estimators of the component distributions and all their functionals.
Semiparametric theory for array-decomposition causal effects remains relatively nascent.
The joint law of observables and the continuously distributed latent variable is identified under three-measurement operator conditions and a labeling restriction.
Triple proxies identify causal functionals by applying continuous full-law recovery, up to an invertible transformation when labels are not normalized.

body.tldr: For every fixed \(K\geq3\), a hidden ordered treatment is recovered from a categorical surrogate, a categorical proxy, and a bounded continuous outcome. The product-bridge influence function is converted into the exact canonical gradient by the pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(N_B=I_{K^{2}}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\) over \(K^{2}\) measurement cells and one conditional Gram solve of dimension at most \(2K^{2}\). Bayes' identity \(R=D^{-1}BW\) gives the equivalent posterior formula without restricting the positive posterior weights. In the separate binary restriction, the exact variance is weakly below the Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen Supplement S8.2 finite-partition variance, and the published refinement sequence converges to the exact bound. An exact symbolic nonconstant-weight \(K=3\) audit and the explicit continuous witness make the finite operator falsifiable and nonzero. The central gate remains the measurable uniformly bounded conditional-\(X\) extension of the constant-\(X\) finite-feature derivative inverse. Efficient cross-fitted inference remains conditional on explicit product rates.

project_justification.gap: The binary hidden-treatment literature characterizes efficiency but computes the continuous-outcome correction through the specific partition-dependent sequence in Supplement S8.2, while the categorical product-bridge literature establishes validity without observed-data canonicality. Existing continuous three-proxy full-law identification does not supply the uniformly bounded derivative inverse needed for tangent completeness.
project_justification.niche: Fixed latent cardinality, quantitative three-view separation, and paired categorical measurements make it possible to eliminate the infinite outcome nuisance pointwise and expose a finite conditional information operator.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the missing DQM tangent-completeness theorem through a constant-\(X\) finite-feature inverse followed by a measurable conditional extension, derives the exact \(D\)-orthogonal finite projector onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\) for fixed \(K\geq3\), proves its Bayes-equivalent posterior representation, relates its binary restriction to the published Supplement S8.2 outcome-partition sequence, supplies an observable strict-gain criterion for adjacent exposure contrasts and an explicit non-binary witness, and attaches coherent cross-fitted inference under explicit nuisance products.

body.related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) are the closest theorem-level comparator. Their Theorems 2--4 give the binary observed tangent space and influence functions. Their Supplement S8.2 continuous-\(Y\) construction partitions \((-L,L]\) into equal-width cells \(I_t^{\ell}\), defines \(p_a^{\ell}(t,X)=P(Y\in I_t^{\ell}\mid J^{\mathrm{bin}}=a,X)\), constructs the conditional-null space \(\mathcal P_1^{\ell}\) and its nuisance-dependent functions \(p_1^{\ell},\ldots,p_{\ell-2}^{\ell}\), and projects on \(V^{\ell}=(B_0p_1^{\ell},B_1p_1^{\ell},\ldots,B_0p_{\ell-2}^{\ell},B_1p_{\ell-2}^{\ell})^{\mathsf T}\). Theorem 4B compares the exact operator only to that verified binary sequence. The multilevel contribution uses the \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\) onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\), which equals the posterior representation after substituting \(R=D^{-1}BW\), followed by one \(2K^{2}\)-dimensional conditional Gram solve. Bian, Zhou, and Cui (2026) inform the raw score through their categorical inverse-feature product bridge and their qualitative nonsingularity and strict modal alignment conditions; none of their assumptions is cited for the proposal-specific uniform \(\varepsilon\) margins. Their Appendix A.8 is not claimed to be improved as a hidden-action policy-value theorem. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009) inform discrete factor identification through Kruskal uniqueness and nonparametric binning. Hu and Schennach (2008) identify a continuous latent full law under three-measurement operator conditions, and Deaner (2023) adapts that level-identification route to triple-proxy causal functionals. Neither continuous full-law recovery result establishes the object required here: first a quantitative right inverse of the constant-\(X\) finite tensor derivative, and then a conditional-\(X\), measurable, uniformly bounded extension that lifts every observed DQM score while preserving support and centering. Tsiatis and Ma (2004) inform the nuisance-score projection strategy in a different functional measurement-error model. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2016) inform coherent repeated-measurement mixture estimation. Tsybakov (2009) supplies the standard H\"older and sieve-rate framework used only to formulate the coherent-fit open question. Guo, Ogburn, and Shpitser (2026) motivate the array-decomposition efficiency gap. Bennett et al. (2023), Ghassami et al. (2026), and Cobzaru et al. (2024) delimit weak-identification, partial-identification, and sensitivity extensions rather than theorem-level targets of this core.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For positive nonconstant \(w\) and full-column-rank \(B\), exact algebra gives \(R=D^{-1}BW\), \(R^{\mathsf T}D=WB^{\mathsf T}\), and equality of the measurement-form and posterior-form projectors. The continuous presolve witness was reproduced with twenty-four quadrature nodes per outcome bin. It has Gram rank twelve, raw-minus-projected covariance eigenvalues approximately \((0.622,1.214,1.589)\), coherent joint perturbation bias of order \(t^{2}\), and vanishing first-order bias under surrogate-only and outcome-only perturbations. The independently differentiated finite quadrature Fisher solve differs from the projector by about \(2.1\times10^{-12}\). These checks are evidence, not a proof that the candidate lies in the full continuous tangent space.
body.honest_scope: The proposal's exact finite projection and canonical-gradient claims are for fixed \(K\geq3\). Proposition 10 and Theorem 4B concern only the separate binary restriction used to reproduce and compare with Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen Supplement S8.2; no arbitrary fixed-basis embedding is asserted. The first cell elimination is fixed as the \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(N_B=I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\) onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\); its posterior expression is used only through the proved identity \(R=D^{-1}BW\). The exact projection, symbolic nonconstant-weight \(K=3\) audit, constant-\(X\) finite-feature derivative inverse, conditional-\(X\) tangent-space equality, partition-sequence variance comparison, pseudoinverse stability, coherent quadratic remainder, empirical-process expansion, and continuous witness membership are all to be proved. The first kill test proves the finite derivative inverse at constant \(X\), then attempts support-preserving recovery for arbitrary bounded common-support class densities; failure of either stage invalidates canonicality. The explicit \(K=3\) law is the non-binary test at which the nine-cell operator is evaluable, has Gram rank twelve, and has nonzero projected correction. The inference theorem is conditional on explicit product rates. Open-ended Question 2 asks whether a tensor-product B-spline product likelihood on \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})\), with \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\), the displayed dimension schedule, and modal-gap label selection, attains the displayed coordinatewise rates for every primitive and derived operator component; those rates are not assumed in the model class or claimed as settled. Modal ties, changing supports, vanishing singular values, and local-to-singularity confidence sets are outside this regular-stratum version. The birth-weight study is a prospective augmented design: the published six-bin application does not itself verify the availability or conditional independence of paired self-report and cotinine measurements. The literature search was bounded and cannot exclude unpublished work, so the strict comparison is confined to accessible public theorem text.
